title: ZBrain TS to Rust Migration
description: Complete ZBrain migration from TypeScript runtime to Rust runtime; JSON is the source of truth and Markdown is the rendered view.

decisions.q: What is the canonical migration strategy?
decisions.answer: Rust is the canonical runtime; TypeScript runtime is a shrinking reference layer. Each Rust slice must prove behavior and delete the corresponding TypeScript implementation/tests/scripts/docs, or record a retention decision.
decisions.note: Based on docs/prd/complete-ts-to-rust.md.

decisions.q: Should 1-2-2 start with audit or implementation?
decisions.answer: Start with a narrow advanced Page writes audit only; do not implement yet.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Audit should compare TS BrainEngine Page-write contract/backend semantics with Rust zbrain-core trait/backends/tests, then split only confirmed gaps into implementation slices.

decisions.q: Which advanced Page-owned capabilities should the 1-2-2 audit focus on?
decisions.answer: Only focus on three confirmed-missing groups: raw data, page versions, and slug/link rewrite.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Raw data covers putRawData/getRawData; page versions covers createVersion/getVersions/revertToVersion; slug/link rewrite covers updateSlug/rewriteLinks. Already-covered soft-delete/tag/refresh/CR-state methods stay out of this plan unless the audit discovers a specific semantic drift.

decisions.q: Should the 1-2-2 audit include Rust schema/migration proposals?
decisions.answer: Yes. Include schema/migration proposals as audit conclusions only; do not implement them in the audit step.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Raw data likely needs raw_data migrations; page versions likely needs page_versions migrations; slug rewrite reuses pages; rewriteLinks may remain no-op parity if TS semantics are no-op. These are planning conclusions for later slices, not immediate implementation.

decisions.q: How complete should Rust public shapes be for raw data and page versions?
decisions.answer: Public shapes should fully align with the TS contract; implementation slices should only cover the three confirmed 1-2-2 behavior groups.
decisions.note: User confirmed. RawData/PageVersion shapes should be complete enough for TS-to-Rust migration parity, while actual implementation/testing remains scoped to raw data, page versions, and slug/link rewrite only; do not expand into upper-layer ingestion/search/facts flows.

1-2-3.label: Move schema migrations ownership to Rust

decisions.q: Does 1-2-3 start with audit/decision only, or does it include full implementation?
decisions.answer: Audit + decision only. First write a canonical schema migrations audit document, define the TS→Rust ownership transfer contract and slice plan; actual implementation moves to child nodes.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q1 = A. Follows the same slice pattern as advanced Page writes: audit document first, then split into focused implementation slices.

decisions.q: What is the parity target for Rust migration capabilities?
decisions.answer: 100% parity. Rust must support all TS migration features: handler functions, verify hooks, sqlFor engine specialization, transaction control, idempotent marking, and drift detection.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q2 = A. Migration parity means no feature regression. The Rust zbrain-core crate must become the single source of truth for all schema migration logic, not a simplified subset.

decisions.q: Where do migration files live after ownership transfer?
decisions.answer: All in crates/zbrain-core/migrations/ and migrations-sqlite/. Rust directories become the single source of truth; TS retains no .sql files, only a calling bridge.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q3 = A. Currently libsql uses migrations-sqlite/ and postgres uses migrations/. These are already the canonical locations for Rust-added tables (files, raw_data, page_versions). This decision extends them to own the entire schema.

decisions.q: How to handle migration version numbering after transfer?
decisions.answer: Reset to Rust-specific versioning. Rust starts fresh at v1, uses a separate rust_schema_version table to track progress, completely avoiding collision with the existing TS user_version.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q4 = B. TS highest version freezes at its current value (~42). Rust migrations run independently, tracked by their own table. Eliminates version-space collision and dual-runner coordination complexity.

decisions.q: What is the transition plan for existing production brains?
decisions.answer: Hard cutover. The next release switches directly to the Rust migration system. TS runMigrations becomes a thin wrapper that only calls Rust init_schema(). No dual-runner transition period.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q5 = A. Aligns with the no-online-users stance. There are no production deployments requiring backward compatibility or staged rollout; hard cutover is both safe and simplest.

1-2-3.notes: ✅ FULLY COMPLETED. All 6 implementation slices finished: audit document, registry foundation, libsql runner, Postgres runner, TS bridge cleanup, final validation. Schema migrations ownership 100% transferred from TypeScript to Rust. Hard cutover complete with zero backward compatibility layer.

1-2-3-2.label: Add Rust Migration registry + runner foundation

decisions.q: Where should the core Migration type live in crates/zbrain-core?
decisions.answer: New dedicated module migration.rs. Standalone module containing only Migration type, registry, and runner foundation.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q1 = A. Follows modular pattern: types.rs for domain types, engine.rs for backend trait, migration.rs for migration-specific abstractions. Shared by both libsql and postgres backends without circular dependency.

decisions.q: Migration dispatch pattern: trait object vs enum?
decisions.answer: trait Migration + dyn object-safe. Each backend implements its own Migration type; unified dispatch via trait object.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q2 = A. Aligns with existing BrainEngine trait pattern. Backend-specific implementations remain in their own modules; shared migration interface in migration.rs. Object-safety is a design constraint the slice explicitly tests.

decisions.q: What Rust type for migration version numbers?
decisions.answer: i64. Directly aligns with SQLite PRAGMA user_version return type; zero conversion overhead.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q3 = B. Pragmatic tradeoff: semantically version numbers should be unsigned, but SQLite PRAGMA returns signed integers. Matching that type eliminates casting at the FFI boundary. Acceptable compromise for lower-level infrastructure code.

decisions.q: How to represent handler/verify signatures in this compile-only slice?
decisions.answer: Stub as unimplemented!() only; defer exact signature definition to node 1-2-3-5.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q4 = B. This slice is compile-only foundation. Handler and verify function signatures depend on BrainEngine trait method availability, which is best finalized during libsql/postgres integration when the calling pattern is concrete.

decisions.q: What object-safety tests belong in this slice?
decisions.answer: Full Migration registry + Migration trait object-safety test. New dedicated test file: engine_object_safety_migration.rs.
decisions.note: User confirmed: Q5 = A. Follows the same pattern as advanced Page writes: explicit compile-only slice with object-safety test as the acceptance gate. Object-safety is a critical design constraint worth its own test file.

1-2-3-2.notes: Compile-only foundation slice. New crates/zbrain-core/src/migration.rs module. Object-safe Migration trait (handler/verify signatures deferred). i64 version numbers. Dedicated object-safety test file. No runner implementation behavior yet.

decisions.answer: One transaction per migration. Each migration runs in its own transaction; failure rolls back only the current migration.

decisions.answer: sql always contains SQLite variant. No specialization override needed for libsql backend; each backend maintains its own migration list.

decisions.answer: Keep SQL exactly as-is, only wrap in new Migration trait. No refactoring, no style changes, zero behavior drift.

decisions.q: What sources should the Page parity audit compare?
decisions.answer: Fix the audit sources to four categories: TS contract, TS backend semantics, Rust contract, and Rust backend/tests.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Do not run an open-ended whole-repo audit for this plan; upper-layer callers such as ingestion/search/facts/takes/agents are out of scope unless a semantic drift deserves a separate sub-node.

decisions.q: What row granularity should the Page parity audit use?
decisions.answer: Use Page contract method / behavior rows, not file-level or module-level rows.
decisions.note: User confirmed. Each audit row should capture TS method/behavior, TS backend semantic notes, Rust trait equivalent, Rust backend coverage, test coverage, status, and follow-up classification.

decisions.q: Should audit status labels have fixed judgment rules?
decisions.answer: Yes. Fix judgment rules for covered, missing, semantic-drift, deferred, and out-of-scope before doing the audit.
decisions.note: User confirmed. covered requires Rust trait equivalent, backend implementation, and tests for key TS semantics; missing means no Rust entry/implementation; semantic-drift means equivalent surface exists but semantics differ; deferred means Page/storage but depends on later slice; out-of-scope means upper-layer flow rather than Page/storage contract.

decisions.q: How should audit follow-up classifications be constrained?
decisions.answer: Do not commit implementation inside the audit document. Use constrained follow-up classifications only: none, sub-node candidate, issue candidate, implementation slice candidate, defer to node 1-2-2, defer to node 1-2-3, or defer to upper-layer roadmap node.
decisions.note: User confirmed. The audit document should provide evidence and classification, not secretly become an implementation plan; concrete work is split after the audit.

1-6-4-5.label: Port magic-link auth (POST issue-magic-link + GET auth/:token with nonce state machine)

decisions.answer: 方案B：独立 MagicLinkAuth struct（nonce 状态机 + LRU pruning），与 AdminAuth 分离。redeem 成功后跨 struct 调用 admin_auth.create_session()。AppState 新增 magic_link: MagicLinkAuth 字段。
decisions.note: 好处：单一职责、独立可测、将来可替换。坏处：多一层 struct + Arc<RwLock，跨 struct 协作。

decisions.q: GET /admin/auth/:token 是否需要 rate limit？
decisions.answer: 需要，端口 TS 的 10 req/min/IP 限制。在 MagicLinkAuth 内部实现滑动窗口计数器 HashMap<IpAddr, Vec<Instant>>。
decisions.note: 不跳过，在 Rust 中实现等效限制。
